topStories.headline: Warfield Commons Opens on Market Street, Giving Mid-Market a Permanent Home for Arts and Media
topStories.dek: KALW Public Media and Community Arts Stabilization Trust open a nine-floor hub at 988 Market St. on September 27, anchoring independent journalism and cultural organizations in the heart of Mid-Market.
topStories.body:
A century-old building at 988 Market Street will open its doors to the public this Sunday as Warfield Commons — a reimagined, nine-floor hub for arts, independent media, and civic organizations that its backers say can help drive Mid-Market's long-sought revival. The free grand opening runs noon to 5 p.m. on September 27, hosted in collaboration with Community Arts Stabilization Trust (CAST), the Tenderloin Community Benefit District, and the Mid-Market Business Association & Foundation.

KALW Public Media, San Francisco's original public radio station, is the building's anchor tenant, occupying two floors for broadcast studios, production and podcast facilities, and a newsroom called the People's Studio. CAST holds majority ownership and will lease the remaining floors at below-market rates to creative organizations, independent journalists, and cultural workers. Tenants already in place include Litquake, the Museum of Performance + Design, the San Francisco Public Press, and the Diasporic Vietnamese Artists Network, among others.

The grand opening will feature cultural performances, local food vendors, building tours led by tenants, artist activations, and a ribbon cutting with elected officials. It also marks the launch of KALW's 'The Next 85 Years' campaign, timed to the station's 85th anniversary, with a fundraising goal of $1 million by December. CAST and KALW purchased the building for $7.3 million in February 2025 using below-market financing from Community Vision Capital & Consultants.

Warfield Commons sits adjacent to the historic Warfield Theatre, steps from Civic Center and the Tenderloin. Mayor Daniel Lurie has called the project a signal of the city's broader comeback. Organizers say the building is already 90 percent tenanted. Note: KALW announced separately that its planned 85th Anniversary Benefit Concert at the Warfield Theatre on September 29 has been canceled due to unforeseen circumstances; the grand opening on the 27th is unaffected.

topStories.headline: Supervisors to Vote on Tenderloin Dog Safety Resolution as Bite Toll Reaches 74 This Year
topStories.dek: The full Board of Supervisors is scheduled to vote this week on Supervisor Mahmood's resolution requiring city housing sites to track dog registrations and report attacks — a response to a surge of bites that has hit the Tenderloin harder than any other San Francisco neighborhood.
topStories.body:
The Board of Supervisors is scheduled to vote Tuesday on a resolution introduced by District 5 Supervisor Bilal Mahmood that would require city-funded shelters and supportive housing sites to maintain registration and vaccination records for resident dogs and report any bites or attacks to the San Francisco Police Department's Vicious and Dangerous Dog Unit through the city's Good Neighbor complaint system. If passed, enforcement is expected to begin next year.

The measure was introduced September 16, one week after an unleashed pit bull-type dog attacked a woman on the 500 block of Larkin Street, leaving her with life-threatening injuries. Officers arrived around 9:20 a.m. to find the dog moving around the injured victim; while restraining it with a catchpole, the dog became unresponsive and died at the scene. The victim was transported to a trauma center and, as of mid-September, remained in serious condition. The dog's owner was not located and no one has been charged.

City data reported by KRON4 shows 74 dog attacks occurred in the Tenderloin between January and September of this year. Mission Local found that 11 of 46 citywide attacks reported in the past 30 days happened in the neighborhood — more than 20 percent of the citywide total from a single district. ABC7's data team reported that Tenderloin dog attacks have doubled over the past three years relative to other city neighborhoods.

Mahmood's resolution also calls for sustained funding for the city's vicious and dangerous dog hearing process — known informally as 'dog court' — which was functionally suspended for nearly a year due to budget shortfalls before the city moved to reinstate it in May 2026. Critics have raised concerns that the new registration and reporting requirements could create additional barriers for unhoused people with pets seeking shelter or housing.

topStories.headline: SF Symphony's 115th Season Is Underway — Renée Fleming Sings Strauss at Davies Hall Starting October 1
topStories.dek: The San Francisco Symphony opened its 115th season with a gala at Davies Symphony Hall on September 24 featuring violinist Hilary Hahn; soprano Renée Fleming joins the orchestra for three Strauss performances next week.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco Symphony launched its 115th season on Thursday, September 24, with an Opening Gala at Davies Symphony Hall featuring violinist Hilary Hahn alongside guest conductor Giancarlo Guerrero. The evening also served as a preview of a season the orchestra is framing as a bridge year — its last before music director designate Elim Chan takes the podium in 2027. Symphony Board President Priscilla Geeslin noted at the gala that Chan already has engagements during the current season, beginning with a program in October.

The season's first star-soloist run follows immediately: soprano Renée Fleming joins the Symphony for a program of Richard Strauss on October 1 (2:00 p.m.), October 3 (7:30 p.m.), and October 4 (2:00 p.m.) at Davies Symphony Hall, 201 Van Ness Avenue in the Civic Center. All three performances are ticketed; information is available at sfsymphony.org.

Other season highlights include composer and conductor Joe Hisaishi leading a West Coast premiere of his Concerto for Orchestra on October 22–23, and former music director Esa-Pekka Salonen returning in April 2027 to conduct a new harp-and-percussion concerto commissioned from composer Rene Orth. The season also includes a January celebration of Conductor Laureate Herbert Blomstedt's 100th year. The full 2026–27 season calendar is at sfsymphony.org.

events.title: SF Good Neighbor Week Kickoff — Civic Center Plaza
events.description: San Francisco's citywide Good Neighbor Week (September 26–October 4) opens with a free celebration at Civic Center Plaza featuring an opening ceremony, a Parade of Neighborhoods, Good Neighbor Award recognition, live music, food trucks, circus performers, and activities for all ages. Now in its second year, the initiative draws on a national holiday started by President Jimmy Carter in 1978.

events.title: Warfield Commons Grand Opening
events.description: Free public grand opening of Warfield Commons, the new arts and media hub anchored by KALW Public Media and Community Arts Stabilization Trust. Includes cultural performances, local food vendors, building tours led by tenants, artist activations, and a ribbon cutting with elected officials. No ticket required; RSVP available on Eventbrite.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack — Free Lunchtime Concerts at Fulton Plaza
events.location: Fulton Street Plaza, 147 Fulton St., Civic Center
events.description: The Civic Center Soundtrack's third season continues with free live music from local artists every Tuesday and Thursday through October, with food trucks on-site. Upcoming performers include Gaby, JW Blunt, and Kevin North on September 29.

events.title: SF Symphony: Renée Fleming Sings Strauss
events.location: Davies Symphony Hall, 201 Van Ness Ave., Civic Center
events.description: Soprano Renée Fleming joins the San Francisco Symphony for three performances of Richard Strauss as part of the orchestra's 115th season. Performances are October 1 at 2:00 p.m., October 3 at 7:30 p.m., and October 4 at 2:00 p.m. Tickets at sfsymphony.org.

events.title: Fall Family Festival at Civic Center Plaza
events.description: A free fall festival under the Spectra lights featuring carnival games, pumpkin decorating, face painting, the SF Public Library Bookmobile, stilt walkers, and bubble magic. Cotton candy, candy apples, and food trucks round out the evening. No ticket required.

moreNews.headline: Tenderloin Police District Boundaries Expand in October
moreNews.body: New Tenderloin Police Station district boundaries approved by the Police Commission last November are set to take effect in October, according to Beyond Chron. The changes — originally projected to begin in July but delayed — will extend the Tenderloin station's coverage northward to Sutter Street and westward to Van Ness Avenue, giving a single station clear jurisdiction over blocks that drug dealers have historically exploited by straddling district lines. The realignment is part of a citywide SFPD boundary overhaul designed to balance officer workloads and improve response times.

moreNews.headline: KALW's September 29 Anniversary Concert at the Warfield Canceled
moreNews.body: KALW Public Media has announced that its 85th Anniversary Benefit Concert at the historic Warfield Theatre — scheduled for Tuesday, September 29 and set to feature BADBADNOTGOOD and Digable Planets — has been canceled due to what the station described as unforeseen circumstances. The grand opening of Warfield Commons at 988 Market Street on September 27 is proceeding as planned. KALW says its broader 'Next 85 Years' anniversary campaign, including future live events and programming, will continue through the year.
